row.scim_plan: Quip Enterprise (SCIM docs; Plus or above inferred)
row.scim_price_text: Contact Sales (Quip Plus lists $25/user/mo billed annually)
row.evidence: Quip's SCIM API reference says "Authorization tokens are only available for Quip Enterprise customers"; the pricing page sells Starter ($10/user/mo) without SSO and puts SSO and the Enterprise API on Quip Plus ($25/user/mo, Contact Sales).
row.notes: New row. Quip (a Salesforce company) lists Starter $10, Plus $25 and Advanced $100 per user/mo billed annually; Plus and Advanced also say Contact Sales. The SCIM docs gate tokens to 'Quip Enterprise customers', a name not used on the current pricing page; mapping it to Plus (which carries SSO and 'Enterprise API') is an inference, so the SCIM price is left as Contact Sales and the multiplier null. SCIM 1.1 and 2.0 at https://scim.quip.com/2 with a bearer token from {company}.quip.com/business/admin/scim; DELETE /2/Users/{id} disables (does not delete) the user and keeps data; groups supported (must have a member). Admin API (users list/lookup, admin roles, session revocation) is documented as available with Quip Advanced or Salesforce Lightning editions, while the pricing page lists 'Enterprise API' on Plus (see conflicts). Events (audit) API is a paid add-on. Okta OIN app is SAML/SWA only; JumpCloud has a SCIM connector. July 2026 release notes add one-click conversion of Quip docs to Slack canvases.

plans.name: Quip Starter
plans.price_text: $10/user/mo billed annually ($12 monthly); $30 for first five users offer
plans.notes: Pricing comparison table marks SSO and Enterprise API & Customization as not included on Starter (page markup).

plans.name: Quip Plus
plans.notes: SSO and Enterprise API listed; SCIM docs say 'Quip Enterprise', not mapped to a tier by Quip; Admin API docs name Quip Advanced, not Plus.

auth.token_expiry: configurable TTL (May 2024 release note on API keys and access tokens)

operations.notes: DELETE /2/Users/{id} disables rather than deletes. v1.1 has no PATCH on /Users; v2.0 has no PATCH on /Groups per limitations list, though the reference also lists 'Patch Groups v2'.

deprovision.data_retained: All data kept; content the user shared stays shared. Separate endpoints remove shared-thread access and transfer private content.
deprovision.notes: Docs suggest toggling active false then true to disable active sessions, implying a plain disable may not end sessions; not stated.

roles.how: SCIM roles field deprecated; admin roles managed through the Admin API.

rate_limits.text: Per-company default of 600 requests per minute (X-Scim-RateLimit-* headers).

limitations.text: Groups must have at least one member; empty-group-then-add flows (e.g. Active Directory) unsupported.
GET /Groups does not support sorting or filtering; groups have no externalId.
userName is set by Quip and cannot be modified.
PATCH on /Groups is not supported in v2.0.

capabilities.notes: User lifecycle is through SCIM; the Admin API reads users and admin roles and revokes sessions/PATs.

endpoints.purpose: Look up user IDs by email
List admin roles for the company

rate_limits.text: Admin API: 100 requests/min and 1,500/hour per user, plus a per-company limit of 600/min.

okta.notes: OIN page (last updated Dec. 18 2018) ticks SAML and SWA only (page markup); no provisioning ticked.
